rows.stem:
Identify the part that controls the closing and opening of the stomatal pore in leaves of plants.

Select the correct option.
rows.solution:
Each stomatal pore is bordered by a pair of guard cells. When water flows into the guard cells they swell and the pore opens; when they lose water they shrink and the pore closes.

This is option (C) Guard cells.

rows.stem: Identify the endocrine gland that regulates the growth of human body.
rows.solution:
The pituitary gland secretes growth hormone, which regulates the growth and development of the body. Too little of it in childhood leads to dwarfism.

This is option (A) Pituitary gland.

rows.stem: Choose the equation of reaction that correctly represents anaerobic respiration in muscles :

options.label: D
options.text: Glucose \(\rightarrow\) Pyruvate \(\xrightarrow[\text{oxygen}]{\text{Lack of}}\) Lactic acid + Energy

rows.solution:
In muscle cells, glucose is first broken down in the cytoplasm to pyruvate. When oxygen is in short supply (during vigorous activity), pyruvate is converted to lactic acid, releasing a small amount of energy. Ethanol and carbon dioxide are the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast, not in muscles.

This is option (D) Glucose \(\rightarrow\) Pyruvate \(\xrightarrow[\text{oxygen}]{\text{Lack of}}\) Lactic acid + Energy.

rows.stem: In human beings, the implantation of fertilised egg takes place in which part of female reproductive system ?
rows.solution:
The fertilised egg (zygote) divides and the young embryo moves down the oviduct to the uterus, where it gets implanted in the thickened, blood-rich lining of the uterus.

This is option (C) Uterus.

rows.stem: When a human egg is fertilized by a sperm having ‘Y’ chromosome, the zygote has the following combination of chromosomes :
rows.solution:
A human egg carries 22 autosomes and an X chromosome (22 + X). A Y-bearing sperm carries 22 + Y. The zygote therefore has 44 autosomes with XY, and develops into a boy.

This is option (C) 44 + XY.

rows.stem: Which of the following is a non-biodegradable pollutant ?
rows.solution:
Paper, wood and vegetable peel are broken down by decomposers, so they are biodegradable. DDT is a pesticide that is not broken down by biological processes and persists in the environment.

This is option (B) DDT.

rows.stem: In an ecosystem, the decomposers perform an important role. Select the option indicating the role of decomposers.

options.label: A
options.text: Convert inorganic materials to simpler forms

options.label: B
options.text: Break down complex organic substances to simple inorganic substances.

options.label: C
options.text: Break down inorganic substances into organic substances.

options.label: D
options.text: Do not act on organic compounds.

rows.solution:
Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down the complex organic substances in dead plants, animals and wastes into simple inorganic substances, which return to the soil and are used again by plants.

This is option (B) Break down complex organic substances to simple inorganic substances.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Bacteria that can withstand heat have better chances of survival in a heat wave.

**Reason (R) :** Accumulation of variations in a species increases the chances of its survival in changing environment.
rows.context: Question No. 8 & 9 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In a heat wave, bacteria that happen to have the variation to withstand heat survive while the others die, so the Assertion is true. Variations accumulated in a species increase its chances of survival when the environment changes, so the Reason is true, and it is exactly why the heat-tolerant bacteria survive.

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The peristaltic movements occur all along the gut.

**Reason (R) :** The lining of the gut has muscles that contract rhythmically to push the food in regulated manner.
rows.context: Question No. 8 & 9 consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Peristaltic movements push food along the whole alimentary canal, from the oesophagus to the intestines, so the Assertion is true. They are possible because the lining of the gut has muscles that contract rhythmically to push the food forward in a regulated manner, so the Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.stem: Give a diagrammatic representation of nutrition in Amoeba.
rows.solution:
Draw four stages of Amoeba, one below the other, joined by arrows:

(a) Amoeba (with its nucleus) near a food particle. Label the nucleus and the food particle.

(b) Amoeba puts out finger-like projections, the pseudopodia, which surround the food particle. Label the pseudopodia.

(c) The pseudopodia fuse round the particle and enclose it in a food vacuole. Label the food vacuole and the food particle inside it.

(d) Inside the food vacuole the food is broken down into simpler substances, which diffuse into the cytoplasm; the undigested material is thrown out at the surface of the cell.

rows.stem: Observe the given figure and identify the labelled parts P, Q, R and S :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the question is to name the parts labelled P, Q, R and S on a printed reflex-arc drawing: a hand held over a steaming vessel, a nerve pathway drawn in red running up the arm to a cross-section of the spinal cord (captioned 'Spinal cord (CNS)', with an arrow captioned 'Message to brain'). Which structure each of P, Q, R and S points at is withheld because it is the answer. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
P: Receptor (the skin of the hand, which senses the heat).

Q: Sensory neuron.

R: Relay neuron (in the spinal cord).

S: Effector (the muscles in the arm).

rows.stem:
Which of the plant hormones are responsible for the following processes ?

(i) Promote cell division

(ii) Inhibition of growth

(iii) Detection of light

(iv) Wilting of leaves
rows.solution:
(i) Cytokinin.

(ii) Abscisic acid (ABA).

(iii) Auxin. No hormone actually detects light, so this part is loosely worded. Auxin is the hormone behind the response to light: when light falls on one side of a shoot, auxin diffuses to the shaded side, the cells there grow longer, and the shoot bends towards the light.

(iv) Abscisic acid (ABA).

rows.stem: Briefly mention the steps in double-circulation through human heart.
rows.solution:
In double circulation the blood passes through the heart twice in each complete cycle:

1. Oxygenated blood from the lungs enters the left atrium, which contracts and pushes it into the left ventricle.

2. The left ventricle contracts and pumps the blood into the aorta, which carries it to the body parts.

3. Deoxygenated blood from the body parts is collected and returned to the right atrium.

4. The right atrium pushes it into the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs for oxygenation.

rows.stem:
Based on Mendel’s experiment show the cross between round, yellow seeds of pea plant (RRYY) with wrinkled and green seeds of pea plant (rryy) upto \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation. Write the number of seeds/plants with following genetic (Genotype) makeup in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation :

(i) RRYY

(ii) rryy
rows.solution:
Parents: round yellow (RRYY) \(\times\) wrinkled green (rryy). Their gametes are RY and ry, so every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant is RrYy, with round yellow seeds.

The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated. Each forms four kinds of gametes, RY, Ry, rY and ry, in equal numbers, giving the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation:

| | RY | Ry | rY | ry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RY | RRYY | RRYy | RrYY | RrYy |
| Ry | RRYy | RRyy | RrYy | Rryy |
| rY | RrYY | RrYy | rrYY | rrYy |
| ry | RrYy | Rryy | rrYy | rryy |

(i) RRYY: 1 (out of 16).

(ii) rryy: 1 (out of 16).

rows.stem:
(a) Mention any one harmful effect of using plastic bags on the environment. Suggest better alternatives to the usage of plastic bags.

(b) Paddy fields require a large amount of water. The pesticides and chemical fertilizers used are washed down into the soil or waterbodies. How do these chemicals reach our bodies ? What is this phenomenon known as ?
rows.solution:
(a) Plastic bags are non-biodegradable, so they persist in the environment for a long time (they also choke drains and harm animals that swallow them). Better alternatives are jute bags or cloth bags (or paper bags).

(b) Pesticides and chemical fertilisers are not biodegradable. They are absorbed from the soil and water by plants, pass into the animals that eat them, and accumulate progressively at each trophic level. Human beings occupy the top level in many food chains, so the maximum concentration of these chemicals builds up in our bodies. This phenomenon is called biological magnification.

rows.stem: Write the structure and function of Bowman’s capsule.
rows.context:
Kidneys help to regulate the volume of fluid and various metabolites waste products in the body.

Normally, kidney filter about 180 L of fluid daily but the volume actually excreted out is only a litre or two a day.

Patients with kidney failures can be saved by dialysis and kidney transplant.
rows.solution:
Structure: Bowman's capsule is the cup-shaped end of the coiled tube (the nephron), enclosing a cluster of blood capillaries.

Function: it collects the filtrate from the blood.

rows.stem: Although kidneys filter a large amount (about 180 L daily) of fluids, still the excretion from the body is only about a litre or two. Why ?
rows.context:
Kidneys help to regulate the volume of fluid and various metabolites waste products in the body.

Normally, kidney filter about 180 L of fluid daily but the volume actually excreted out is only a litre or two a day.

Patients with kidney failures can be saved by dialysis and kidney transplant.
rows.solution: As the filtrate flows along the tubular part of the nephron, most of the water, along with useful substances such as glucose, amino acids and salts, is selectively reabsorbed into the blood in the surrounding capillaries. Only a litre or two of urine is left to be excreted.

rows.stem: What is excretion ? Why is it necessary for any living organism ?
rows.context:
Kidneys help to regulate the volume of fluid and various metabolites waste products in the body.

Normally, kidney filter about 180 L of fluid daily but the volume actually excreted out is only a litre or two a day.

Patients with kidney failures can be saved by dialysis and kidney transplant.
rows.solution:
Excretion is the process by which the harmful metabolic wastes, such as the nitrogenous wastes urea and uric acid, are removed from the body.

It is necessary because these waste products are toxic; if they were allowed to accumulate they would harm the organism, so their removal is essential for survival.

rows.stem: State two similarities between lungs and kidneys.
rows.context:
Kidneys help to regulate the volume of fluid and various metabolites waste products in the body.

Normally, kidney filter about 180 L of fluid daily but the volume actually excreted out is only a litre or two a day.

Patients with kidney failures can be saved by dialysis and kidney transplant.
rows.solution:
Any two:

1. Both remove metabolic wastes from the blood: the lungs remove carbon dioxide, and the kidneys remove nitrogenous wastes such as urea.

2. Both have thin-walled blood capillaries, which take part in the exchange of gases (lungs) and the filtration of blood (kidneys).

rows.stem:
(i) In an angiospermic flower, fertilization is said to take place when male gametes carried in the pollen tube fuse with the female gamete, present in the embryo sac. This results in lot of changes in different parts of the flower. State the changes taking place in the following structures of flower post fertilization :

(a) Zygote

(b) Ovule

(c) Ovary

(d) Sepals

(ii) Define germination.
rows.solution:
(i) (a) Zygote: it divides several times to form an embryo within the ovule.

(b) Ovule: it develops a tough coat and is gradually converted into a seed.

(c) Ovary: it grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit.

(d) Sepals: they shrivel and fall off.

(ii) Germination is the process in which a mature seed develops into a seedling under appropriate conditions (water, air and suitable temperature).

rows.stem:
(i) Sugarcane does not produce seeds so name the process through which it will be able to reproduce.

(ii) List any two advantages of this method.

(iii) Besides sugarcane, give two more examples of plants that reproduce by this method.

(iv) Why regeneration is not possible in all the types of animals ?
rows.solution:
(i) Vegetative propagation (sugarcane is grown from stem cuttings).

(ii) Any two:

1. Plants raised by vegetative propagation bear flowers and fruits earlier than those produced from seeds.

2. The new plants are genetically similar to the parent plant, so its desirable characters are kept.

3. Plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds can still be propagated.

(iii) Any two: rose, grapes, banana, orange, jasmine.

(iv) Regeneration is carried out by specialised cells, which divide to form a mass of cells that then develop into the different tissues. Only organisms that have such cells can regenerate; most complex animals, with highly differentiated cells, do not have them, so regeneration is not possible in all animals.

rows.stem: The volume ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated during electrolysis of water is :
rows.solution:
In the electrolysis of water, hydrogen is liberated at the cathode and oxygen at the anode:

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

Two volumes of hydrogen form for every one volume of oxygen, so the ratio is 2 : 1. This is option (B) 2 : 1.

rows.stem: Which of the following set of compounds does \(\underline{\text{not}}\) belong to same homologous series ?
rows.solution:
Members of a homologous series have the same general formula. \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\), \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\), \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\) and \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\) all fit \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\) (alkanes). But \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) fits \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\) (an alkene), so it is not in the same series as \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\).

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) and \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\).

rows.stem: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide ?
rows.solution:
Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases to give salt and water. \(\mathrm{Na_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2O}\) are basic oxides and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is an acidic oxide, while aluminium oxide reacts with both:

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O}\)

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).

rows.stem:
Study the following table and select the correct option :

| Option | Salt | Acid used | Base used | Nature of Salt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (A) | \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) | \(\mathrm{HCl}\) | \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) | Basic |
| (B) | \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\) | \(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\) | \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) | Neutral |
| (C) | \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}\) | \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) | \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) | Acidic |
| (D) | \(\mathrm{CH_3COONa}\) | \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) | \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) | Basic |
rows.solution:
A salt of a strong acid and a strong base is neutral; of a strong base and a weak acid, basic; of a strong acid and a weak base, acidic.

Sodium chloride (HCl with NaOH) and sodium sulphate (\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) with NaOH) are neutral, and sodium carbonate (weak carbonic acid with NaOH) is basic, so the first three rows are wrong. Sodium acetate comes from the weak acid \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) and the strong base NaOH, so it is basic.

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{CH_3COONa}\); \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\); \(\mathrm{NaOH}\); Basic.

rows.stem: Which of the following will \(\underline{\text{not}}\) undergo addition reaction ?
rows.solution:
Addition reactions take place only in unsaturated compounds, which have double or triple bonds. \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) (alkenes) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\) (an alkyne) are unsaturated. \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\), propane, is a saturated alkane with only single bonds, so it does not undergo addition.

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Four solutions, namely fructose, ethanol, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide filled in four separate beakers are connected one by one in an electric circuit with a bulb. The solutions in which the bulb will glow when current is passed are :
rows.solution:
The bulb glows only when the solution contains ions to carry the current. Hydrochloric acid gives \(\mathrm{H^+}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) ions in water, and sodium hydroxide gives \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) and \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions. Fructose and ethanol do not form ions in solution, so they do not conduct.

This is option (D) hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide.

rows.stem: Which gas is evolved when magnesium metal reacts with very dilute \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) ?
rows.solution:
Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent and usually oxidises the hydrogen formed to water. But magnesium (and manganese) react with very dilute nitric acid to give hydrogen gas:

\(\mathrm{Mg + 2HNO_3 \rightarrow Mg(NO_3)_2 + H_2}\)

This is option (C) Hydrogen.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Reaction of quick lime with water is an exothermic reaction.

**Reason (R) :** A large amount of heat is evolved on the reaction of quick lime and water.
rows.context: In the question two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and other labelled as Reason (R). Answer this question selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Quick lime reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime, releasing a large amount of heat:

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

A reaction in which heat is evolved is exothermic, so the Assertion is true. The Reason states that a large amount of heat is evolved, which is true and is exactly why the reaction is called exothermic.

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
Define the following terms :

(i) Olfactory indicator

(ii) Water of crystallization
rows.solution:
(i) Olfactory indicators are substances whose odour changes in acidic or basic media (for example onion, vanilla essence and clove oil).

(ii) Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt (for example, 5 in copper sulphate, \(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O}\)).

rows.stem:
What happens when

(i) lead (II) nitrate is heated ?

(ii) iron (II) sulphate is heated ?

(iii) silver chloride is exposed to sunlight ?

Write balanced chemical equations of the reactions involved in support of your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) Lead(II) nitrate decomposes on heating, giving off brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide and leaving lead(II) oxide; oxygen is also released.

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

(ii) The green crystals of iron(II) sulphate first lose their water of crystallisation; on further heating the solid decomposes to brown iron(III) oxide, and a smell of burning sulphur is noticed.

\(\mathrm{2FeSO_4(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Fe_2O_3(s) + SO_2(g) + SO_3(g)}\)

(iii) White silver chloride turns grey in sunlight as it decomposes to silver and chlorine.

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

The marking scheme awards full marks for the balanced equations alone.

rows.stem:
(a) Give the chemical name and formula of Plaster of Paris.

(b) Write the chemical equation of its preparation.

(c) Give any two uses of it.
rows.solution:
(a) Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}\).

(b) It is prepared by heating gypsum at 373 K:

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O \xrightarrow{373\,K} CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + \frac{3}{2}H_2O}\)

(c) Any two: for supporting fractured bones in the right position; for making toys and materials for decoration; for making surfaces smooth.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
(a) Name the acid present in ant’s sting.

(b) Give reason :

(i) While diluting an acid, it is recommended that the acid should be added to water.

(ii) Baking soda is used as an antacid.
rows.solution:
(a) Methanoic acid (formic acid), HCOOH.

(b) (i) Mixing an acid with water is highly exothermic. When the acid is added slowly to water, the heat is spread through the large volume of water and there is no excessive local heating. If water were added to the concentrated acid instead, the heat could make the mixture splash out and cause burns, and the glass container could break.

(ii) Baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate) is alkaline in nature, so it neutralises the excess acid in the stomach and gives relief:

\(\mathrm{NaHCO_3 + HCl \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O + CO_2}\)

rows.stem: Write structural formula and name of 4th member of alcohol homologous series.
rows.context: Alcohol forms a homologous series with general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\)–OH and –OH group as functional group. Ethanol is commonly called alcohol and is used in alcoholic drinks. It is good solvent, used in medicines, cough syrups, tonics etc.
rows.solution:
The alcohol series is methanol, ethanol, propanol, butanol. The fourth member is butanol (butan-1-ol), \(\mathrm{C_4H_9OH}\):

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)

(In the full structural formula, four carbon atoms are joined in a chain, each carbon carries the hydrogen atoms that complete its four bonds, and the end carbon carries the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group.)

rows.stem: What happens when ethanol is heated with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) ? Write chemical equation involved.
rows.context: Alcohol forms a homologous series with general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\)–OH and –OH group as functional group. Ethanol is commonly called alcohol and is used in alcoholic drinks. It is good solvent, used in medicines, cough syrups, tonics etc.
rows.solution:
Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid. Alkaline potassium permanganate acts as the oxidising agent.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4 + \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

rows.stem: Write the chemical equation of reaction of ethanol with ethanoic acid in the presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\). Write the name of this reaction.
rows.context: Alcohol forms a homologous series with general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\)–OH and –OH group as functional group. Ethanol is commonly called alcohol and is used in alcoholic drinks. It is good solvent, used in medicines, cough syrups, tonics etc.
rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + H_2O}\)

Ethanoic acid and ethanol react in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form the sweet-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate and water. This reaction is called esterification.

rows.stem: What happens when ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K ? Write chemical equation involved. What is the role of concentrated sulphuric acid in this reaction ?
rows.context: Alcohol forms a homologous series with general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}}\)–OH and –OH group as functional group. Ethanol is commonly called alcohol and is used in alcoholic drinks. It is good solvent, used in medicines, cough syrups, tonics etc.
rows.solution:
Ethanol is dehydrated to ethene:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\,K} CH_2=CH_2 + H_2O}\)

Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent: it removes water from ethanol.

rows.stem:
(i) Give reasons for the following :

(I) Ionic compound have generally high melting points and boiling points.

(II) Solder, an alloy of lead and tin, is used for welding electrical wires.

(III) Carbon cannot reduce the oxides of Na or Mg.

(ii) The reaction of compound ‘X’ with aluminium is used to join railway tracks :

(I) Identify the compound ‘X’.

(II) Name the reaction.

(III) Write the balanced chemical equation of the reaction of compound ‘X’ with aluminium.
rows.solution:
(i) (I) In an ionic compound the oppositely charged ions are held by strong inter-ionic forces of attraction, and a considerable amount of energy is needed to break them. So ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.

(II) Solder has a low melting point, so it melts easily and can be used to join electrical wires without damaging them.

(III) Sodium and magnesium have more affinity for oxygen than carbon has, so carbon cannot remove oxygen from their oxides. These metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction instead.

(ii) (I) X is iron(III) oxide, \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\).

(II) The thermit reaction.

(III) \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_2O_3(s)}\) + heat

The marking scheme deducts half a mark if the equation is not balanced.

rows.stem:
(i) Write the balanced chemical equations when :

(I) A mixture of \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) is heated.

(II) \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) is heated in the presence of oxygen.

(ii) Give reasons for the following :

(I) The wires carrying current in homes have a coating of PVC.

(II) To make hot water tanks, copper is used and not steel.

(iii) Show the formation of ionic compound \(\mathrm{CaO}\) with electron dot structure.

[Atomic number : Ca = 20, O = 8]
rows.solution:
(i) (I) Copper(I) oxide reacts with copper(I) sulphide to give copper:

\(\mathrm{2Cu_2O + Cu_2S \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 6Cu(s) + SO_2(g)}\)

(II) Zinc sulphide is roasted to zinc oxide:

\(\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

The marking scheme deducts half a mark if an equation is not balanced.

(ii) (I) PVC is an insulator, so the coating insulates the current-carrying wires and protects against shocks and short circuits.

(II) Copper does not react with cold water, hot water or steam, so the tank does not corrode, while steel (mostly iron) rusts in contact with hot water. Copper is also a better conductor of heat than steel.

(iii) Calcium (2, 8, 8, 2) has two valence electrons; oxygen (2, 6) has six. The calcium atom transfers its two valence electrons to the oxygen atom:

\(\mathrm{Ca \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2e^-}\) and \(\mathrm{O + 2e^- \rightarrow O^{2-}}\)

In the electron dot diagram, Ca is drawn with two dots, O with six crosses, and arrows show the two electrons moving from Ca to O. The product is written \(\mathrm{[Ca^{2+}][O^{2-}]}\), with the oxygen showing a complete octet inside its brackets.

rows.stem: Rays from the sun converge at a point 25 cm behind a convex lens. The distance at which an object be placed in front of the lens to get a virtual image, is :
rows.solution:
The sun's rays are parallel and converge at the principal focus, so the focal length is 25 cm. A convex lens forms a virtual (erect, enlarged) image only when the object is between the optical centre and the focus, that is, closer than 25 cm. Of the choices, only 20 cm is less than 25 cm.

This is option (A) 20 cm.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: To restore clear vision in persons whose size of the eye ball has reduced, he/she is suggested to use suitable
rows.solution:
When the eyeball becomes too small, the image of a nearby object forms behind the retina; this is hypermetropia (far-sightedness). It is corrected by a convex lens, which converges the rays a little before they enter the eye.

This is option (A) Converging lens.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The needle of a magnetic compass kept in strong external magnetic field, always aligns itself in north-south direction on the earth.

**Reason (R) :** Behaviour of the needle of a compass is same as that of a freely suspended bar magnet.
rows.context: For question number 32, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to this question from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A compass needle sets along the magnetic field acting at its position. In a strong external magnetic field it aligns along that field, not along the north-south direction of the earth's field, so the Assertion is false. The needle of a compass is a small magnet and behaves like a freely suspended bar magnet, so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
(a) Relate the speed of light in the given medium with its optical density.

(b) Using the information given in the table below, arrange the medium A, B and C in the ascending order of their optical density.

| Medium | Speed of light (m/s) |
|---|---|
| A | \(2.25 \times 10^8\) |
| B | \(2 \times 10^8\) |
| C | \(2.08 \times 10^8\) |
rows.solution:
(a) The speed of light is greater in an optically rarer medium and smaller in an optically denser medium: the higher the optical density, the lower the speed of light.

(b) The speeds are A \(2.25 \times 10^8\) m/s, C \(2.08 \times 10^8\) m/s and B \(2 \times 10^8\) m/s. The fastest medium is the least dense, so the ascending order of optical density is A \(<\) C \(<\) B.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
(i) How does the change in curvature of the eye lens helps us in the process of seeing the nearby objects clearly ?

(ii) State the range of the power of accommodation of a normal human eye.
rows.solution:
(i) To see a nearby object, the ciliary muscles contract, so the eye lens becomes thicker and its curvature increases. Its focal length decreases, and the image of the nearby object is focused on the retina.

(ii) The question asks for the range of the power of accommodation, but what is expected is the range of vision of a normal eye: from 25 cm (the near point) to infinity (the far point). Over this range the eye lens adjusts its focal length so that each object is focused on the retina.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: Draw a ray diagram to show the correction of eye defect of an old man who can not see an object placed closer than 1 m from his eye, clearly.
rows.solution:
The old man cannot see objects closer than 1 m, so his near point has moved away to 1 m (hypermetropia, here presbyopia). It is corrected with a convex lens.

Diagram: draw the eye with its lens and the retina. Mark the normal near point N' at 25 cm and the defective near point N at 1 m, farther from the eye. Draw a convex lens in front of the eye. Rays from an object at N' pass through the convex lens and are bent so that they appear (dotted lines) to come from N; the eye lens then focuses them on the retina. Draw arrows on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark for not showing the direction of light.

(For such a lens, \(u = -25\) cm and \(v = -100\) cm, so \(\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = -\frac{1}{100} + \frac{1}{25} = \frac{3}{100}\); \(f = \frac{100}{3}\) cm and the power is \(+3\) D.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
(a) Draw the ray diagram for refraction of light through a glass prism and mark angle of refraction and angle of deviation.

(b) When the path of a light ray refracted through a glass prism is reversed how will the angle of deviation change ? Explain.
rows.solution:
(a) Draw a triangular glass prism. A ray (incident ray) falls obliquely on one refracting face; draw the normal there. On entering the glass the ray bends towards the normal; the angle between this refracted ray and the normal is the angle of refraction, r. At the second face the ray bends away from the normal and leaves as the emergent ray. Produce the incident ray forward and the emergent ray backward (dotted) until they meet; the angle between them is the angle of deviation, D. Label r and D and put arrows on the rays.

(b) The angle of deviation does not change. Light follows a reversible path, so the reversed ray simply retraces its original path through the prism: it enters along the old emergent ray and leaves along the old incident ray, and the angle between those two lines is the same.

rows.stem:
(a) A ray of light after reflection from a concave mirror becomes parallel to its principal axis. Draw a labelled ray diagram to show this.

(b) (i) Differentiate between the virtual images formed by a convex mirror and concave mirror.

(ii) “The value of magnification ‘*m*’ for a mirror is \(-2\).” Calculate the height of object if the height of image is 20 cm.
rows.solution:
(a) Draw a concave mirror with its pole P, principal focus F and centre of curvature C on the principal axis. Draw a ray passing through F towards the mirror; after reflection it travels parallel to the principal axis. Label P, F, C and the principal axis, and put arrows on the incident and reflected rays.

(b) (i) Any one difference:

| Virtual image by a convex mirror | Virtual image by a concave mirror |
|---|---|
| Formed for all positions of the object | Formed only when the object is between the pole and the principal focus |
| Diminished | Enlarged |

(ii) \(m = \frac{\text{height of image}}{\text{height of object}} = \frac{h'}{h} = -2\). The negative magnification means the image is real and inverted, so its height is taken as \(h' = -20\) cm.

\(h = \frac{h'}{m} = \frac{-20}{-2} = 10\) cm.

The object is 10 cm high.

rows.stem:
(a) Why does an electric bulb become dim when an electric heater in parallel circuit is switched ON ?

(b) How to connect three resistors each of resistance \(8\,\Omega\), so that the equivalent resistance of the combination is \(12\,\Omega\) ? Draw diagram of the combination and justify your answer.
rows.solution:
(a) When the heater is switched on in parallel, it draws a large current from the supply. As a result the current through the bulb decreases, and the bulb glows dim. This happens only because the supply and the connecting lines have some resistance of their own, which the question does not mention: the large heater current causes a larger voltage drop across that resistance, leaving less voltage across the bulb. With an ideal supply the voltage across a bulb in parallel would not change.

(b) Connect two of the resistors in parallel and the third in series with this pair.

Diagram: two \(8\,\Omega\) resistors side by side between points A and B, and the third \(8\,\Omega\) resistor between B and C.

Justification: for the parallel pair, \(\frac{1}{R_1} = \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{4}\), so \(R_1 = 4\,\Omega\). Adding the third in series, \(R_{eq} = R_1 + 8 = 4 + 8 = 12\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: If the ammeter reading is X ampere with nichrome wire of length ‘*l*’, then what will be the ammeter reading if the length of nichrome wire is doubled with same area of cross-section ?
rows.context:
Three students Shweta, Ayesha and Samridhi were performing an experiment to understand the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends. Each one of them completed electric circuit with the help of a cell, an ammeter, a plug key and wire.

Shweta put nichrome wire of length ‘*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Ayesha put nichrome wire of same thickness but twice the length i.e. ‘2*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Samridhi took copper wire of length ‘*l*’ and same thickness in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.
rows.solution: Resistance is proportional to length, so doubling the length doubles the resistance. With the same cell, the current is halved: the ammeter reads \(\frac{X}{2}\) ampere.

rows.stem: What happens to the ammeter reading if the area of cross-section of nichrome wire is doubled, keeping the length of wire ‘*l*’ the same ?
rows.context:
Three students Shweta, Ayesha and Samridhi were performing an experiment to understand the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends. Each one of them completed electric circuit with the help of a cell, an ammeter, a plug key and wire.

Shweta put nichrome wire of length ‘*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Ayesha put nichrome wire of same thickness but twice the length i.e. ‘2*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Samridhi took copper wire of length ‘*l*’ and same thickness in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.
rows.solution: Resistance is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section, so doubling the area halves the resistance. The current doubles: the ammeter reads 2X ampere.

rows.stem: Define ‘resistivity’. Write its SI unit. Compare the resistivity of an alloy with its constituents metals.
rows.context:
Three students Shweta, Ayesha and Samridhi were performing an experiment to understand the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends. Each one of them completed electric circuit with the help of a cell, an ammeter, a plug key and wire.

Shweta put nichrome wire of length ‘*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Ayesha put nichrome wire of same thickness but twice the length i.e. ‘2*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Samridhi took copper wire of length ‘*l*’ and same thickness in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.
rows.solution:
The resistance of a conductor is \(R = \rho\frac{l}{A}\). Resistivity \(\rho\) is the resistance of a conductor of the material of unit length and unit area of cross-section.

Its SI unit is the ohm metre, \(\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\).

The resistivity of an alloy is generally higher than that of its constituent metals.

rows.stem:
Give reason :

(i) Tungsten is used almost exclusively for making the filament of electric lamps.

(ii) Conductors of bread-toasters are made of an alloy rather than a pure metal.
rows.context:
Three students Shweta, Ayesha and Samridhi were performing an experiment to understand the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends. Each one of them completed electric circuit with the help of a cell, an ammeter, a plug key and wire.

Shweta put nichrome wire of length ‘*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Ayesha put nichrome wire of same thickness but twice the length i.e. ‘2*l*’ in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.

Samridhi took copper wire of length ‘*l*’ and same thickness in the circuit and after plugging the key, noted current in the ammeter.
rows.solution:
(i) Tungsten has a very high melting point (about 3380 \(^\circ\)C), so it does not melt when the filament becomes white hot; it also has a high resistivity.

(ii) The resistivity of an alloy is generally higher than that of its constituent metals, so it produces more heat; and alloys do not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw a diagram showing the magnetic field lines around a bar magnet. Write any two characteristics of magnetic field lines.

(ii) Write the statement of Right hand thumb rule.

(iii) The concentric circles representing the magnetic field around a current carrying straight wire become larger and larger as we move away from the wire. How does magnetic field change on these concentric circles ?
rows.solution:
(i) Diagram: draw a bar magnet marked N and S. Draw closed curves leaving the north pole, going round outside the magnet and entering the south pole, with arrows pointing from N to S outside the magnet; the lines are crowded near the poles and spread out farther away.

Any two characteristics:

1. Field lines emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole outside the magnet; inside the magnet they run from the south pole to the north pole, so they are closed curves.

2. The relative strength of the field is shown by the closeness of the field lines: they are crowded where the field is strong.

3. No two field lines cross each other.

(ii) Right-hand thumb rule: imagine holding a current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.

(iii) The magnetic field decreases as the concentric circles become larger, that is, it becomes weaker with distance from the wire.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
(i) Draw a diagram, showing the magnetic field lines in and around the current carrying solenoid. Write any two salient features of these lines.

(ii) What is an electromagnet and how is it made ?
rows.solution:
(i) Diagram: draw a solenoid connected to a cell and a key. Inside the solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines along the axis; outside they curve round from one end to the other, so that one end behaves as a north pole and the other as a south pole. Put arrows on the lines.

Salient features:

1. The pattern of the field lines of a solenoid is similar to that of a bar magnet.

2. The field lines inside the solenoid are parallel straight lines, showing that the field is uniform there.

(ii) An electromagnet is a magnet made by passing an electric current through a coil wound on a piece of magnetic material such as soft iron; it behaves as a magnet only while the current flows.

It is made by winding a coil of insulated copper wire around a soft iron core (that is, placing soft iron inside a current-carrying solenoid) and passing a current through the coil.
